requirement:
Node-insertion methods queue selections. They resolve no contents or edges,
render no inputs, and record no observations while building.

Awaiting with a configured agent resolves these selections in call order:

| Insertion | Contents delivered |
| --- | --- |
| `contents_of_current_node()` | The node identified by `ValidationContext::node_id`. |
| `contents_of_successors(label)` | Targets of edges whose labels equal `label`, in returned edge order, including duplicate targets. |

Each successful successor selection records its source, label, and target-set
fingerprint, even when nothing matches. Only selected targets have their contents
resolved. Each delivered node is recorded with its supplied snapshot's
fingerprint under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.author_procedure`.
Input-resolution failures return `ValidationError::Graph`.
rationale:
The three marked tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/validation.rs` cover every obligation of `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.node_contents`.

- **Queueing only while building.** `dropped_builders_and_missing_agents_do_not_resolve_queued_inputs` builds a builder with `contents_of_current_node().contents_of_successors(7)` and drops it. It then asserts that `inspection().dependencies()` is empty. It also awaits a builder with no agent configured and expects `NoAgentConfigured`. Finally it asserts that the `Memory` helper recorded no content reads and no edge selections. The graph was set to fail edge lookups, so any resolution would have shown up. `queued_reads_selection_and_rendering_fail_before_agent_invocation` also drops a builder and asserts that the agent received no request.
- **Call order, current node, and successor targets.** `explicit_insertions_preserve_order_repetition_and_selection_snapshots` queues current, successors(7), then current again. The edges are `[(7,3),(8,99),(7,2),(7,3)]`. It asserts that the agent receives `[1, 3, 2, 3, 1]` with the matching contents. This shows call order, edge order, duplicate targets kept, and the label-8 edge excluded. It also asserts that the graph's `reads` equal `[1,3,2,3,1]`, so only selected targets are resolved. The current-node content comes from the node id `1`.
- **Selection and node records.**
  - The same test asserts the full dependency list: `Dependency::OutgoingEdges(1, 7, edge_fingerprint(&[2,3]))`, then `Node(1, fp("subject"))`, `Node(3, ...)` and `Node(2, ...)`. This covers the source, label and target-set fingerprint. It also covers per-node fingerprints, with repeated nodes recorded once.
  - `queued_reads_selection_and_rendering_fail_before_agent_invocation` covers the empty-match cases. These are no edges at all, and only a non-matching label. In both, the successor selection is awaited and the test asserts there were no content reads. The only dependency is `OutgoingEdges(1, 7, edge_fingerprint(&[]))`.
- **Input-resolution failures.** The same test makes the content read fail, then the edge lookup fail, then the render step fail. It expects `ValidationError::Graph("read")`, `Graph("edges")` and `Graph("render")` respectively. In the render case it asserts that no dependencies were recorded and that the agent request count is unchanged.

The `Memory` helper (`outgoing_edges`, `node_content`) pushes to `selections` and `reads` and fails on the flags, so the assertions are meaningful. The `author_procedure` citation (node identities and fingerprints recorded) is exercised by the dependency assertions. I found no unacknowledged gap, and there are no {fixme} acknowledgments.

Node-insertion methods queue selections. They resolve no contents or edges,
render no inputs, and record no observations while building.
Awaiting with a configured agent resolves these selections in call order:
| Insertion | Contents delivered |
| `contents_of_current_node()` | The node identified by `ValidationContext::node_id`. |
| `contents_of_successors(label)` | Targets of edges whose labels equal `label`, in returned edge order, including duplicate targets. |
Each successful successor selection records its source, label, and target-set

:::{req} author_procedure
A `Criterion::execute` invocation receives one `Send + Sync`
`ValidationContext<'d, D>` for `D: Domain`, with tracked `inspection(&self)`
and the `ask(&self)` builder under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge`.
Each awaited ask builder runs its own conversation and returns its own submitted
answer. The context combines delivered node contents, tool reads, direct
inspection reads, and recorded edge selections into one dependency trace for
the criterion. It records the node identities and fingerprints of the supplied
contents. A later call that selects fewer nodes, or none, preserves earlier
inputs. An unawaited builder contributes no
agent-delivery dependencies.
Shared references support concurrent calls: builders, conversations, and
submission state remain independent, while updates to the trace are synchronized.
Calls can run concurrently without holding an exclusive context borrow across
an agent interaction or locking the whole context for the conversation.
The same context supports deterministic criteria under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation.criterion_trait`.
